title: Extended Care Health Option (ECHO) Service Authorization and Payment of Claim Lines
content:
1. Every Extended Care Health Option (ECHO) service needs an authorization from the case manager covering the service kind, provider and month, valid for the authorization validity period in months; services that a public facility could provide need a public facility use certification for beneficiaries aged the certification minimum age or older.
2. A claim line is paid only when an ECHO authorization for its service kind and provider covers its month.
3. ECHO services are authorized only on a registration whose status is registered.

The authorization validity period and the minimum age for the public facility use certification are the figures of the product's covered services and authorization standards.

## What an authorization records

An ECHO service authorization is given by the ECHO case manager for one service kind, starting in one month, on one registration. It records the beneficiary, the service kind authorized, the first and last months covered, the hours authorized per month (0 for services that are not hourly), and the authorized ECHO provider.

## Clause 2 in detail: matching a claim line

A claim line is paid only when there is, on the line's own registration, an ECHO authorization whose service kind is the line's service kind, whose provider is the line's provider, and whose months from first to last include the line's month of service. The match is read from the authorization records on file before the line is paid.

| Service kind matches | Provider matches | Line's month within the authorization's first to last month | Line paid under clause 2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | yes | may be paid |
| yes | yes | no | not paid |
| yes | no | yes | not paid |
| no | yes | yes | not paid |

## Clause 3 in detail: the registration's status

An ECHO service is authorized only on a registration whose status is registered, as the registration record shows before the authorization is given. A registration that is applied, denied, closed at the family's request or closed for loss of eligibility does not have the status registered.

## Hypothetical cases, for illustration only

- An authorization for respite care with one provider covers March through August. A respite care line from that provider for June meets clause 2; a line from that provider for September does not; a respite care line from a different provider for June does not.
- An authorization for training does not cover a transportation line in the same month.
